docs/how-forge-works.html.tool-flow: export + checkTools{{tools}} registered tools ({{auto}} auto + {{onDemand}} on demand), as defined by packages/mcp-server/src/tools/registry.json: compose, validate, render, code, charts, dashboards, certify, tokens, catalog.
docs/how-forge-works.html.trait-format: A trait file has a named header (trait:). Across the authored inventory, its {{traitSectionCount}} section names are {{traitSectionRoster}}; each trait uses the sections it needs. The table below explains the core sections using Stateful as the example:
docs/how-forge-works.html.trait-states: From that, Product gains a status field restricted to those {{productStateCount}} values, a transition history, and a computed list of next states; every Product list shows a status badge, every detail page a status timeline, every form a status selector whose options come from the object's own states. Parameters flow into component props (optionsParameter: states), so the same StatusSelector is correct for Product's {{productStateCount}} states and Subscription's {{subscriptionStateCount}}. Parameter values are checked against each trait's JSON Schema (schemas/traits/<name>.parameters.schema.json) when the full engine resolves an object — pnpm object:validate, object:compose, object:generate; the tools' lighter composer merges without validating, so run object:validate after editing an object.
docs/how-forge-works.html.domain-traits: The {{domainTraitsWord}} SaaS-billing traits live in a domain pack (domains/saas-billing/) — a folder of traits and objects for one vertical that the engine loads alongside the core set. That is the mechanism for adding a new domain without touching core traits.
docs/how-forge-works.html.product-fields: • Fields are merged — every trait's schema fields plus the object's own: {{productFields}} fields for Product. If two traits declare the same field, the full engine applies collision rules (same type → merge, keep the stricter; two enums → union; required beats optional; different types → error unless the object resolves it) and records which trait each field came from.
docs/how-forge-works.html.product-parameter-type: • Parameters are applied — validated against each trait's schema, and parameter-driven enums become real constraints (Product's generated TypeScript type has status: {{productStatesType}}).
docs/how-forge-works.html.composer-semantics: The full engine (src/core, src/registry; the object:* commands) performs the composition steps above. The tools' runtime composer (packages/mcp-server; what object show and design.compose use) merges schema, semantics, view extensions and tokens only — last-wins on collisions with a warning, no parameter validation — and orders extensions higher-priority-first (default {{runtimePriority}}), where the React view engine orders lower-first (default {{viewPriority}}).
docs/how-forge-works.html.object-title: 05The object inventory ({{objectDefinitions}} definitions; {{objectNames}} unique names)
docs/how-forge-works.html.object-homes: Each of the {{objectDefinitions}} definitions has one home: objects/ for the core set, or a domain pack for its vertical. objects/ is scanned before domains/, and a later shipped file that repeats a name is reported and not served. Adding an object is a new *.object.yaml file (the suffix is required) in objects/ or a domain pack; the loaders index once per process, so it appears on the next server start.
docs/how-forge-works.html.context-roster:
Context

The kind of screen an object is being shown in. A trait's view extension names the context it targets, so the same object produces a different — but consistent — screen for each. Traits contribute to list, detail, form, timeline, card and inline. Bound bar and line traits also author dashboard contributions, selected through the public dashboard layout. The chart view remains a shell.
docs/how-forge-works.html.region-roster: Every context in Forge's component library is laid out on the same {{regionsWord}} named regions, in this order: {{regionRoster}}. Main is always required; page header is required in every context except card and inline; list and timeline also require the toolbar. Regions render as real HTML landmarks (nav, header, main, aside with labels), so structure is visible to screen readers and testable.
docs/how-forge-works.html.view-assembly: How a screen is assembled. For the requested context, Forge collects every trait's extensions, sorts them by priority (lower first, default {{viewPriority}}; ties by declaration order), evaluates any conditions (data, permissions, theme), groups them by region and composes them in a fixed order. Each rendered piece is wrapped in a boundary carrying its id, region and source trait, and a debug mode prints a per-region report. Below tablet width ({{tabletWidth}}px container) the two-column contexts collapse to one column; an opt-in drawer component turns the side panel into a focus-trapped sheet.
docs/how-forge-works.html.renderer-layouts: The React view engine uses the component library and region contract above. The tools share one HTML document renderer between code.generate and repl: it binds the composed object’s sample record, renders component styles, native form controls, tab panels and chart SVG, and uses layout templates — {{renderLayouts}} — with named slots. Static HTML is a sample screen with local controls and integration notices for domain actions. It has no {{regionsWord}}-region responsive application shell; browser coverage is measured separately.
docs/how-forge-works.html.component-counts: The canonical intake contains {{components}} unique component claims. The historical reconciliation proposal classified {{historicalRuntime}} as runtime component rows ({{historicalNative}} native and {{historicalRecipes}} recipes) and {{historicalAuthoring}} as non-runtime authoring-only rows. The retained review accepted all 109 obligations; the set was later expanded to include VizGraphPreview, and then Switch and Dialog; the old {{historicalRuntime}}-runtime split remains unapproved and approvedRuntimeCensus stays null. Missing implementations remain obligations. Historical component evidence marks exactly {{foundationReact}} React and {{foundationVue}} Vue surface cells as foundation-v1-candidate; a separate independent review accepted those candidates and a distinct authorization promoted all {{foundationPromoted}} to foundation-v1. That promotion does not approve the {{historicalRuntime}}-row runtime census. That historical foundation nucleus is {{foundationRoster}}. The current evidence measures {{reactComponents}} React and {{vueComponents}} Vue implementations, {{htmlComponents}} HTML render functions (function presence alone does not prove rendered semantics), and {{contracts}} versioned contracts. {{governedComponents}} of the {{components}} are governed: each has {{governedDefinition}}. The generated apps of the latest runtime sweep use {{placedComponents}} of them; the ledger's proven-in-generated-apps label still comes from the retained reviewed sweep. Accessibility is verified for {{accessibleComponents}} rows and theme for {{themedComponents}} rows; interaction is verified for {{interactiveComponents}} and explicitly not applicable for {{staticComponents}} static rows. No framework row is unavailable. These are measured component scenarios and bounded runtime receipts; that historical review is complete. The authored shared scenario roster contains {{scenarios}} scenarios. The generated capability ledger and date-tagged catalog export agree. The current proposal is {{nativeComponents}} native, {{recipeComponents}} recipe and {{aliasComponents}} alias; all {{components}} classifications await the owner’s approval; the earlier independent review did not approve the classification proposal. catalog.list filters the catalog by category, trait or context; object show returns an object's composed traits and extensions.
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-outputs: One build (pnpm build:tokens, Style Dictionary) compiles the JSON sources into {{tokenOutputs}} outputs: CSS custom properties ({{tokenVariables}} variables), a TypeScript map, a Tailwind token map, a Swift file and a Kotlin file. Tokens are layered so that a change at the right level propagates:
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-themes: Themes are light, dark and high-contrast (the last maps to the operating system's forced colours). Brands are made from a recipe (a neutral, an accent, which of them the primary action takes, a radius and a font) into values for the brand colour roles — surfaces, text, interactive, borders, status and focus — the brand's radius and font, and its chart palettes, one JSON file per brand per theme (the base files contain {{tokenLeaves}} leaves each, under brands/<X>/{base,dark,hc}.json). The build emits a block per brand × theme that re-assigns {{bridgedSlots}} shared theme slots to that brand's values:
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-brands: So switching brand or theme is two attributes on the document; no component changes. {{brandCountWord}} brands ship today ({{brandRoster}}); {{presetCountWord}} brand-relative presets ({{presetRoster}}) ship with the token package as starting points. brand.intake makes a brand from a team's own values: its template lists every slot with its meaning and a starting value (an existing brand's, or a preset over it), validate reports every problem (missing slots, colours that do not parse, the brand contrast rules in each theme) and writes nothing, and create writes a brand that validates into the team's brands folder (from npm, ~/.oods-foundry/brands) and builds it there, outside the runtime, or into a source checkout's token package. In a source checkout, brand.apply previews a change to a brand, checks the brand as the change would leave it, or writes canonical brand source and runs both token-build stages, retaining source hashes, byte counts and captured build results in a dated review folder. A failed build reports the output tail and leaves source writes in place. From the runtime, brand.apply with apply rebuilds a team's brand in its brands folder and writes only a review kit for the shipped brands. With apply: true, tokens.build compiles current registry source using the shipped compiler kit in isolated artifact storage, returns requested-scope CSS variables, CSS and JSON inline, and writes those values alongside the full CSS and legacy A/light TypeScript and Tailwind files. It never changes the shipped runtime. Preview writes nothing.
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-guards: Guards around the build. A collision guard refuses to build if two source files declare the same token with different values; {{brandContrastRules}} brand-contrast rules ({{brandContrastPairs}} pairs per brand per theme: text, icons, control borders and the focus ring) run before every release (the guardrails suite in pnpm run a11y:release), and any theme slot a brand newly overrides must be graded; a real-browser check asserts the computed values in all {{brandThemeCells}} brand × theme cells; a token-governance diff (pnpm run tokens:governance) reports high-risk token changes by namespace and segment; it blocked them as a pull-request gate, unless the pull request carried the token-change:breaking label, while hosted CI ran, and is run by hand now that it does not.
docs/how-forge-works.html.generation-path: The generate path is four stages that chain — compose, validate, render and generate — with pipeline running them together. They pass a UiSchema between them:
docs/how-forge-works.html.ui-schema-shape:
UiSchema

A JSON tree of components. The schema declares node properties {{uiNodeProperties}} and root properties {{uiRootProperties}}. Traits' token maps are carried into tokenOverrides.
docs/how-forge-works.html.compose-tool: design.composeAn object + context ({{composeContexts}}), or a short intent that names one ("product detail page"); an intent that names no object returns an unbound layout chosen from keyword tables, optional layout ({{composeLayouts}}) and component overrides.A UiSchema plus a reference id ({{ttlMinutes}}-minute lifetime), placed-component selections, reasons and warnings. Confidence is omitted when no measured score exists. Object-aware: it fills slots from the object's fields and view extensions and reports which traits it used.
docs/how-forge-works.html.validate-tool: repl · validateA UiSchema, or a patch to one (JSON Patch or per-node replace).Structural validation against the schema grammar and component catalog; optional shared-renderer HTML checks and declared component CSS contrast pairs across every built brand/theme.
docs/how-forge-works.html.codegen-tool: code.generateA validated UiSchema; framework {{frameworks}}; styling {{styling}}; TypeScript on/off.A single-screen schema returns source code plus its import list; a workflow returns application files. React imports the real @oods/components-react package, Vue imports @oods/components-vue, and both import @oods/component-styles/css. A known component/target pair that is not emission-eligible fails before emission with typed error OODS-N015 and no source payload; HTML remains standalone.
docs/how-forge-works.html.schema-lifetime: schema · save/load/list/deleteA schema reference.Persists work past the {{ttlMinutes}}-minute reference lifetime and across sessions.
docs/how-forge-works.html.product-screen: Intent matching is rule-based (keywords and synonyms choose the layout; a deterministic selector picks components), so the same input always produces the same tree — there is no language model inside Forge. A real run: intent "product detail page" auto-detects the Product object, picks the detail layout, and returns a {{productNodes}}-node tree. Its selections name {{productSlots}} filled slots, {{productTabs}} of them tab slots; the returned screen places {{productSlotsOnScreen}} of them ({{productSlotsOnScreenRoster}}), with {{productTabPhrase}} holding Product's fields as read-only rows. The selected slot roster is {{productSlotRoster}}.
docs/how-forge-works.html.fidelity-and-datasets: fidelity.preview draws declared object relationships as a boxes-and-arrows SVG, or a labelled component-containment diagram from a schema. It renders composed wireframes with regions, authored text and field bindings; review adds only recorded confidence. Branded mockups use static sample HTML in the selected built brand/theme. These drawings are not live applications or referential-integrity checks. The legacy Object Catalog input and nine packaged fixtures remain supported, with legacy branded mockups using a built brand's light tokens; brand-a/brand-b class-name aliases remain for one release. The map tool stores trait annotations and validated component substitutions in a user folder; compose records substitutions and generated React and Vue import the mapped implementations, with advisory contract reports. Unmeasured obligations remain not checked. New catalog identities are not supported by substitution. structuredData.fetch serves live components, objects and traits including registered definitions, plus archived token data; registry.snapshot serves recorded mappings and active definitions with shadowing diagnostics. Historical draft records are not advertised as snapshot capabilities. Explicit version requests preserve historical exports.
docs/how-forge-works.html.portable-outcomes: The retained portable E2E records outcomes for {{portableTools}} advertised tools on the packaged runtime built at {{portableBundleHead}} (a builder's receipt). {{portableOutcomeSentence}} {{runtimeLimitSentence}} brand.apply previews from the shipped brand source and, with apply, emits its review kit without writing the bundle. The native code is preserved at tools/call. The selected tool receipt records which tokens.build operation ran and what it verified; readiness attestations bind React/Vue generation to shipped package bytes. The separate extracted-bundle reference-app ledger, measured on the archive built at {{releaseArchive}} and not this build, records {{releaseCells}} cells across {{releaseApps}}, {{releaseContexts}} contexts in {{releaseFrameworks}}: {{releasePass}} pass, {{releaseTyped}} typed gaps, and {{releaseEqual}} generated artifacts equal the corresponding host hashes.
docs/how-forge-works.html.viz-taxonomy: The versioned taxonomy classifies {{taxonomyIdentities}} chart identities ({{taxonomyTypes}} types and {{taxonomyPatterns}} patterns, {{taxonomyRetiredPatterns}} of them retired and not offered) across {{taxonomyFamiliesWord}} families and records active Core Analytics Profile cells as surface-complete or typed gaps, with retired cells and their reasons recorded separately.
docs/how-forge-works.html.viz-vocabulary: viz.render takes data and returns a chart specification. {{chartTypesWord}} chart types: {{cartesianRoster}} (from tabular rows; compiled to Vega-Lite, ECharts on request) and {{primaryRoster}} (from node/link/geometry inputs; ECharts). Four input modes: a catalog pattern identity, explicit (chart type + encodings), suggest (rows only — the recommender picks), or a structured intent (goal, measures, dimensions). Pattern mode uses bundled authored data and presentation; scenes preserve layers, bounded facets and secondary axes, retired patterns are not offered (the input schema refuses one with OODS-V001; a caller that skips the schema gets OODS-V174 with the reason), and unsupported data structures return OODS-V167, and conflicting explicit operands return OODS-V166. The {{cartesianCountWord}} Cartesian families return spec; the {{primaryCountWord}} ECharts-primary families omit spec and return echartsSpec with output.echarts forced true and reason echarts-primary-family. Every successful result carries a content hash of the canonical spec; on request it also returns an accessible data table and a generated narrative derived from the same data. The {{vizTraits}} viz-category traits (marks, encodings, scales, layouts, interactions, scatter composition and geocoding) are the vocabulary the spec is normalised into. Temporal axes and adapter-generated formatted date parsing use UTC, independent of the host timezone. Caller-authored expressions retain their own semantics. ScaleTemporal declares no timezone parameter; rendering uses UTC; numeric tooltips use en-US.
docs/how-forge-works.html.dashboard-vocabulary: dashboard.render composes a metric overview — KPI tiles, a trend panel, a breakdown panel, optional geo — from shared datasets and panel definitions, with deterministic auto-layout, applies a caller-supplied cross-filter selection at render time (links are returned as given and change nothing), and can export one self-contained HTML file with server-rendered SVG for its {{dashboardTypes}} admitted chart types in light, dark and high contrast: Vega-Lite for the {{cartesianCountWord}} Cartesian families and ECharts for {{dashboardPrimaryWord}} primary families. Chord and flow_map remain excluded from the public dashboard panel schema (#881). Governed measureRef resolution defaults to true; unknown refs return OODS-V130 and missing fields return OODS-V137. Explicit resolveMeasures:false disables that resolution. Failed panels retain explicit error placeholders; a successful chart panel must have a renderable specification. KPI tiles in the HTML export draw computed sparklines and labelled breach and anomaly markers.
docs/how-forge-works.html.certify-pillars:
Certify

artifact.certify takes a chart specification back (and, for the advanced types, its data) and returns a per-check scorecard plus a combined conformance result on the declared certification path. Its {{certifyPillarsWord}} core certification pillars are accessibility equivalence, determinism, contrast and accuracy.
docs/how-forge-works.html.a11y-rule-count: Accessibility equivalence{{a11yRules}} structural rules over the chart and its text alternative: colour encodings carry a second cue and size differences are perceptible; an accessible table exists, captioned to the chart title, with declared column order; axis titles, an accessible name and a description at least {{a11yDescriptionMinimum}} characters are present; bar/stacked charts narrate extrema, trend charts narrate the trend, area charts describe their baseline/range; datasets with {{a11yFindingsRowMinimum}}+ rows surface at least {{a11yFindingsMinimumWord}} findings and dense ones aggregate; every encoded field is present in every row; the narrative generator reports ready; interactions describe their announcements. Each rule names its precondition; absent preconditions remain visible as not applicable. On the data-backed ECharts path, error-severity failures fail the accessibility pillar and conformance; warning-severity findings remain visible without failing the pillar.
docs/how-forge-works.html.determinism-scope: DeterminismTwo independent compiled or projected specifications are canonicalised and byte-compared, then independently rendered SVGs are compared. Content and render hashes identify the corresponding viz.render output for the same operand and scope; notes retain any rendering limitation and the certified runtime boundary.
docs/how-forge-works.html.contrast-thresholds: ContrastThe colour values actually baked into the spec are graded: every mark at least 3:1 against the requested light or dark theme canvas (WCAG 1.4.11); categorical palettes checked for distinguishability under normal vision and three colour-vision-deficiency simulations; gradient scales reported as exempt, not passed. The requested brand and light/dark/hc theme are retained. High-contrast returns an exempt contrast result with reason forced-colors and no numeric grade; the browser resolves the declared system colours.
docs/how-forge-works.html.accuracy-rule-count: Accuracy{{accuracyRules}} reader-only structural-distortion rules: bar baseline not at zero (or on log/sqrt); dual y-axes in one frame; area on a non-linear scale; a row-merging aggregation not disclosed in title, description or axis; negative treemap/sunburst values; a parent not equal to the sum of its children; negative sankey/chord links; sankey node height inconsistent with its flows; duplicate sankey links; conflicting values joined to one map region; invalid bubble sizes and flow strengths, radius-based bubble scaling, duplicate geographic operands, and overlapping duplicate directed force-graph links. Reciprocal links remain distinct. "Pass" means no offered rule detected its distortion, and the count of rules that actually ran is reported. ECharts accuracy requires at least one evaluated rule; missing preconditions never count as a pass.
docs/how-forge-works.html.certify-scope: Coverage, stated plainly. The {{cartesianCountWord}} Cartesian types certify from their IR. Advanced types use the declared operand profile with the same data supplied to rendering: conformance requires accessibility to pass, contrast to be neither failed nor ungradeable, stable determinism, and evaluated-and-clean accuracy. Certified coverage can carry a measured false conformance result. Spec-only ECharts calls remain uncertified with null conformance and a missing-operand explanation; this path adds no Vega-Lite compile. Certification covers chart specs, not pages or components. It accepts any brand in the brand registry and theme light, dark or hc (defaults A/light), matching rendering and contrast grading. Measured SVG rendering and certification cover 13 chart types across 78 brand/theme scopes (A/B × light/dark/hc). High-contrast contrast grading is exempt with reason forced-colors, not a numeric contrast pass. Forced-colours browser evidence covers chart SVGs, dashboard HTML and the React/Vue Subscription detail preview.
docs/how-forge-works.html.token-contrast: • Accessibility checks — a11y.scan and opt-in repl validate/pipeline grade declared component CSS foreground/background pairs using current built tokens for every brand/theme, including team brands. Given a screen, they inspect its shared-renderer HTML for language/title, main landmark, IDs and ARIA references, names/labels, image alternatives, chart SVG metadata and heading order. Unresolved inherited surfaces, dynamic CSS, alpha compositing and OS colours remain unmeasured. No browser-computed colour/layout, keyboard/focus or screen-reader claim.
docs/how-forge-works.html.browser-viewports: • Local accessibility release gate — pnpm run a11y:release runs the {{brandContrastRules}} brand-contrast rules, root accessibility and component axe suites (including spatial), token validation, a fresh Storybook build, its curated light/dark axe check, and phone ({{phoneWidth}}), tablet ({{tabletWidth}}) and desktop browser checks. Browser axe uses WCAG 2.2 AA tags and fails serious/critical findings; the curated legacy Storybook check excludes colour-contrast and has separate token-pair contrast grades. The desktop form and imported/generated application proofs include browser colour-contrast. Receipts retain failures and skipped tests; the gate does not update baselines. Chromatic visual regression remains optional.
docs/how-forge-works.html.operating-roster: Start and connect. Build the server once: pnpm --filter @oods/mcp-server run build. Connect an AI assistant with the stdio adapter: docs/runtime/install.md carries the Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor steps for the released runtime bundle, and configs/agents/ holds the same three generated config snippets for a clone. For a browser panel or HTTP-style agents, run the bridge (pnpm bridge:dev; it listens on 127.0.0.1:{{bridgePort}}). From the terminal, call any tool directly: pnpm exec tsx tools/oods-agent-cli/src/index.ts plan design.compose '{"intent":"product detail page"}'. The authoritative roster is packages/mcp-server/src/tools/registry.json: {{auto}} tools register by default and {{onDemand}} more switch on with MCP_TOOLSET=all.
docs/how-forge-works.html.safety-model: Safety model. brand.apply's source edits and build, map create and apply, a11y.scan's report need apply: true, tokens.build, brand.apply and a11y.scan preview calls write nothing; their applied calls write the run record (transcript and bundle index); map update and delete and schema save and delete write immediately; design.compose records a composition version per call unless transient, design.preview's edit and accept record versions, code.generate writes files in file payload mode, and pipeline writes via its save option. {{rolesWord}} roles ({{roleRoster}}); per-tool rate limits, concurrency and timeouts from a policy file; run records land under artifacts/current-state/<date>/ with redacted transcripts and a hashed bundle index; the write paths the policy declares are informational, not enforced. Optional OpenTelemetry tracing per tool call.
docs/how-forge-works.html.generation-targets: • Code generation targets React, Vue and static HTML. HTML documents embed sample data, component styles and local controls; domain actions display an integration notice. Build validation checks contracts and fallback absence without running the document. Browser measurement is a separate proof.
docs/how-forge-works.html.native-token-scope: • Typography is each brand's own: its sans and mono stacks, emitted in every brand scope. The categorical chart palette resolves by brand and theme and accepts explicit token overrides. The Swift/Kotlin files carry one default brand × theme and omit font stacks and easing curves.
docs/how-forge-works.html.footer: Figures are generated from the Forge repository ({{traits}} traits · {{objectDefinitions}} object definitions / {{objectNames}} unique names · {{components}} governed component claims · {{contexts}} contexts · {{chartTypes}} chart types). The {{tools}}-tool roster comes from packages/mcp-server/src/tools/registry.json; contracts: packages/mcp-server/src/schemas/ and docs/api/.
docs/how-forge-works.html.state-machine-cardinality: • Tokens, semantics, actions and a state machine (multiple owners are refused by default) are merged.
docs/how-forge-works.html.stateful-extension-example: view_extensionsWhich UI piece to show in each context, where, and with what props.list: StatusBadge · detail: StatusTimeline (top, priority {{statefulDetailPriority}}) · form: StatusSelector · timeline: StateTransitionEvent · card: StatusBadge

docs/how-forge-works.html.release-evidence-limit: health reports built token scopes and a labelled configured defaultScope, not an observed consumer scope. design.preview serves the generated app through the preview host on 127.0.0.1 (the bridge in-process, or the host the stdio adapter starts); without a reachable host it returns OODS-N021. Release-profile receipts from code.generate and pipeline carry evidenceVerification: file-verified-not-re-executed. {{releaseEvidenceLimit}} Request dslVersion and repl.output.depth were removed because no handler consumed them; UiSchema.version remains.
docs/how-forge-works.html.object-chart-runtime-limit: Charts inside generated objects. Subscription draws one bar per recorded payment in detail, its amount axis in the record's currency. Invoice declares a bar chart over line_items with money metadata (minorUnits and currencyField), so each line item's amount plots in major units on an axis in the invoice's currency, summing matching descriptions. Usage declares a temporal line chart over samples: the record's own readings, its y axis titled with the record's unit label (titleField: unit_label). A bar is at most 48px thick, so one or a few categories no longer fill the plot. Invoice and Usage author detail and dashboard placements. Trait title and description parameters travel with the chart. React and Vue application generation and HTML chart-node generation use actual renderer SVG; Static HTML tab panel trees preserve nested content and layout. Static HTML keeps labelled actions with honest integration notices; list controls and tabs operate locally and form inputs retain edits in the open page. No domain action changes a backend record. These passive sample assets stay fixed when a local record is edited, and consumers can supply a replacement SVG. The capability inventory observes composed declarations; generated-application runtime proof is recorded separately. Relationship declares a force graph in detail and workflow through MarkGraph and VizGraphPreview. Its optional neighborhood array charts the record and the relationships that share one of its endpoints, titled Connected relationships. The edge-array transformation sorts distinct node IDs, retains source-to-target row order, adds a reverse link only for a true bidirectional flag, and deduplicates directed pairs without inventing weights or groups. The named wrapper preserves the native ECharts SVG. This ungrouped example has no categorical semantic metadata: light/dark contrast is ungradeable even though accuracy and determinism pass; HC contrast is exempt. Browser proof checks visible marks and labels in every scope. The inventory observes 10 declarations across 4 chart types. The other seven ECharts types remain unplaced: treemap and sunburst need hierarchy arrays; sankey and chord need numeric link values; choropleth, bubble_map and flow_map need inline geometry and their corresponding region, point or flow values.

docs/concepts.md.canonical-regions:

docs/concepts.md.token-architecture:
### 1. Four-Layer Token Architecture (conceptual)

This diagram illustrates four design roles. It is not a count of implemented token namespaces; the modifier layer is a conceptual role.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Modifiers Layer (--mod-*)          │  ← Runtime variants (hover, focus, disabled)
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Component Layer (--cmp-*)          │  ← Component-specific tokens
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Theme Layer (--theme-*)            │  ← Light/dark, brand overlays
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Reference Layer (--ref-*)          │  ← Foundational design tokens
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The illustration recommends component-level aliases. The current build also includes system tokens; component implementations may reference those shared roles directly.
docs/concepts.md.quintet-example:
### Universal Quintet Pattern
The original modeling guide groups these examples into a “Universal Quintet.” This is a design vocabulary, not a measured prevalence claim:

1. **User/Person**: Authentication, authorization, identity
2. **Product/Item**: The "things" your system manages
3. **Transaction/Event**: State changes, business events
4. **Organization/Location**: Structural, spatial context
5. **Relationship/Association**: Many-to-many connections

README.md.schema-ttl: - `schemaRef` TTL: refs returned by `design_compose`, `design_preview`, `pipeline_run`, and `schema_store` (`action: load`) last {{ttlMinutes}} minutes inside the server process that issued them; a client keeps that process for one conversation, and a restarted client starts a new one that does not know earlier refs (`OODS-N003`). Persist them with `schema_store` (`action: save`) when the workflow spans sessions or multiple review loops, and load them by name with `action: load`.
README.md.what-forge-is:
OODS Forge is a design-system engine that an AI assistant drives over MCP. You name a screen by its object and its context; Forge composes the screen from governed components and tokens, generates it as React or Vue code, renders charts and dashboards from your data, and certifies the charts it renders against accuracy, accessibility, contrast and determinism rules. It installs from npm (`npx -y @oods/foundry`) as a local MCP server for Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor.

Today it knows {{objectNames}} objects, {{traits}} traits and {{governedComponents}} governed components, renders {{chartTypes}} chart types under a taxonomy of {{taxonomyPatterns}} named patterns, and advertises {{auto}} tools by default ({{tools}} in all). A governed component has {{governedDefinition}}; the generated apps of the latest runtime sweep use {{placedComponents}} of the {{components}}.
README.md.three-words:
- **Object**: a thing your product has, described once with its fields and behaviours. `Subscription` is an object: a plan, a status, a billing interval and a payment history. Forge ships {{objectNames}} objects, each defined in YAML; a team adds its own objects the same way, in its own folder (`~/.oods-foundry/objects` from npm), and the `object_registry` tool validates and registers them without a restart.
- **Trait**: a capability an object composes in, bringing its fields, states and screen contributions with it. `Subscription` composes `Stateful` (a status with allowed transitions) and `Billable`; `User` and `Organization` compose `Addressable`. There are {{traits}} traits, {{vizTraits}} of them chart traits; a team's own traits go in its own traits folder and place only the components Forge ships.
- **Context**: the kind of screen an object is shown in. The same `Subscription` produces a different but consistent screen for each of {{composeContexts}}; a trait's view extension says what it contributes to which context.
README.md.generates-and-certifies:
Forge generates React and Vue code from composed screens: a screen as a component, or a whole workflow application. Its static HTML output shows sample data, working local controls and labelled domain actions that disclose the need for application integration. It opens from disk; generation checks are static and browser coverage is measured separately. Every component comes from the {{governedComponents}} governed components and every colour, space and type value from the token system. {{brandCountWord}} brands ship today, each with light, dark and high-contrast themes. It renders {{chartTypes}} chart types from your data ({{cartesianRoster}} from tabular rows; {{primaryRoster}} from node, link and geometry inputs) and composes dashboards of KPI tiles, trend, breakdown and map panels over {{dashboardTypes}} admitted chart types, as tokened SVG and specs.

"Certify" is a measurement, not a promise. `artifact_certify` takes a chart specification Forge rendered and runs its {{certifyPillarsWord}} pillars on it: accuracy ({{accuracyRules}} structural-distortion rules about baselines, hidden aggregation, mis-scaled encodings and inconsistent structure; a chart is graded on the ones that apply to its type, and the result names them), accessibility equivalence (the narrative and the data table say what the chart says), contrast (the drawn paints against the tokens) and determinism (two independent renders hash the same). Each pillar reports pass or fail with findings, or says why it was not graded (unchecked, ungradeable or exempt), and `coverage` says whether the chart type is on the certified path. Certification covers chart specifications only, never a screen, an application or a page. Generated screens carry a `validationReceipt` from `code_generate` naming the static checks that ran (schema structure, component registry, state contract, target readiness, dependency closure and more; nothing is compiled or run) and, under `notChecked`, the ones that did not. No receipt claims a check it did not run.
README.md.first-run-health: The default surface is {{auto}} tools; `MCP_TOOLSET=all` adds the {{onDemand}} on-demand tools, {{tools}} in all. `health_check` reports the tool ledger's {{tools}} entries by where the specs that import each tool live, not by what they proved, and not the surface your client lists.
